set.typical_award_size: Fee-based program that replaced the former inclusionary ordinance (Ordinance 2000 of 2021; Chapter 25.45 amended by Ordinance 2046, adopted March 2, 2026; Chapter 25.44 was not amended). Residential impact fee on residential floor area with a credit for existing uses; exempt are rental projects of 10 or fewer units and for-sale projects of 6 or fewer. FY 2026-27 Master Fee Schedule rates per square foot (lower rate in parentheses where prevailing or area wage is paid): rental 11 units and above $17 ($14) up to 50 du/ac, $21 ($17) at 51 to 70 du/ac, $31 ($26) at 71 du/ac and above; for-sale 7 units and above $36 ($31). On-site alternative allowed as of right: rental projects providing 10% low income plus 5% very low income units in perpetuity, or for-sale projects providing 15% low income units for 55 years, are deemed mitigated; off-site units, preservation conversions, land dedication or other alternatives need Council approval. Commercial linkage fee (Chapter 25.44) on hotel, retail, restaurant, service and office projects adding 5,000 square feet or more: retail $7 ($5), hotel $12 ($10), office up to 50,000 square feet $18 ($15), office over 50,000 square feet $26 ($21) per square foot. Both fees feed the Affordable Housing Fund (about $12 million as of the July 2025 NOFA).
set.next_deadline: Not applicable; fees are due before the first building permit at the schedule in effect when the permit issues, and an affordable housing plan is required with the first application when the on-site or other alternative is used. No open round as of November 10, 2026.
set.affordability_requirement: On-site alternative units: rental 10% low plus 5% very low income in perpetuity; for-sale 15% low income for 55 years; built concurrently with market units, square footage equal to or greater than market units, finishes at least 60% of market value, same amenities; regulatory agreement recorded. Density bonus projects pay the fee on all market-rate units, including bonus market-rate units, but not on affordable units, with a reduction to the extent affordable units mitigate impacts. Council may waive fees for public or nonprofit public benefit uses.

set.typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Projects of 7 to 50 units: for-sale 15% (5% above moderate, 5% median, 5% moderate), rental 20% (5% low, 5% median, 10% very low or Housing Choice Voucher and other subsidy recipients). Projects over 50 units: 20% for both tenures (for-sale 10% above moderate, 5% moderate, 5% median). In-lieu fees are required from projects of six or fewer units or lots, from new commercial and industrial development over 1,000 square feet (a commercial linkage fee) and from condominium conversions; fees are set by Council resolution and indexed annually at 50% of the Santa Cruz-Watsonville House Price Index change, paid at building permit or final map (14-46.070). FY 2025-26 schedule (effective July 1, 2025, Resolutions 238-01, 72-12 and 136-23): $21,885 per single-family detached unit, $8,419 per multifamily unit for projects of six or fewer units or lots, and $1.75 per square foot for commercial and industrial floor area of 1,001 square feet or more. Income categories use the Watsonville median household income, defined as 70% of the Santa Cruz County median. Federal, state or City-assisted affordable projects meeting the percentages satisfy the chapter in full (14-46.040(c)). Projects with 50% or more affordable units receive priority processing (14-46.080). Release fees for de-restricting units are paid into the affordable housing fund.
set.next_deadline: Not applicable; requirement applies at entitlement. No application round as of November 10, 2026. In-lieu fee amounts are in the City's FY 2025-26 affordable housing in-lieu fee schedule; a FY 2026-27 update was not located.
